body_markdown:
At Sonoco, we believe our responsibility extends beyond producing sustainable packaging. Throughout the company, we support the communities in which we live and work through focused, intentional giving and volunteer efforts. As our guiding principle states, ‘people build businesses by doing the right thing,’ and we’re doing our part to strengthen the children and families who live within our surrounding communities.


### **Enriching Communities Through Sonoco In Action**


Sonoco In Action is a dedicated arm of the Fortune 500 company that invests in the people and places that shape our teams and workplaces. Through volunteerism and dedicated funds of approximately $2 million, we invest in enriching community:


- Education
- Health and wellness
- Arts and culture
- The environment
- Disaster relief


This charitable Sonoco arm serves the community by:


- **Offering grants to non-profit organizations** like the Sonoco Employee Relief Fund, which gives financial assistance to employees impacted by a natural disaster, family emergency or unexpected event.
- **Sponsoring company events and activities** like the Pee Dee Heart Walk, which raised over $27,000 for the American Heart Association in 2025—earning Sonoco a Top Fundraising Company Per Capita in Pee Dee award!
- **Organizing community engagement activities** like our Positive Advocates Working with Students (PAWS) and our Youth to Leader programs, which provide opportunities to mentor students ages 18 and under during school hours.


### **Investing in Youth and Families Local to Sonoco**


Each year, Sonoco partners with local schools to build confidence, develop life skills and strengthen students’ overall well-being.


We recently talked to a few of our very own PAWS and Youth to Leader mentors to hear about their experiences.


#### Hearing From Positive Advocates Working With Students (PAWS) Mentors


**Senior Specialist for Legal Entity Records and Intellectual Property Management, Geneva King** has mentored her student mentee for almost four years. For King, becoming a PAWS mentor was personal. She elaborated, “I’ve had a firsthand experience of seeing how hands-on help can make a difference, and I wanted to do the same for others.”


King recalled connecting with her mentee over sharing the same favorite color and the color of her mentee’s hair, pink. She pointed to the importance of putting in the time, consistently showing up and being patient as being the key to her special mentorship relationship.


While every student participated in PAWS for a different reason, King supported her mentee with tutoring sessions, advice on how to pursue future career aspirations and assistance with navigating family challenges and relationships.


Throughout the mentorship, King shared that she’s not only gained confidence personally but also learned how to better appreciate what she has and the impact she has been able to make. To others considering becoming a PAWS mentor, she encouraged, “Whatever you can do to help, lean in.”


**Continuous Improvement Emerging Leader, Gavin Gainey** began his mentorship one year ago. After receiving an email about the PAWS program, he immediately wanted to help. He explained, “As someone who had the experience of positive mentors, I wanted to give back.”


Gainey’s elementary-school mentee struggled with reading. With the help of his mentee’s teacher, they set a milestone to finish a book in a popular book series. As a result of spending time together a few times each month and supporting this reading goal, his mentee was not only able to finish that book but also several more in the series.


This mentorship is rewarding for Gainey too. He reported, “You learn from the kids too.” A two-way street, PAWS mentoring has enabled him to both be and have a bright spot in life.


### **Hearing From the Youth to Leader Coordinator and Mentors**


**Associate Human Resources Manager, Halli Crouch** recalls running into a grandmother of a Youth to Leader mentee while having a flat tire repaired. As the primary caretaker of the elementary-school student, this grandmother shared the impact the Youth to Leader program made on her family. Crouch shared, “Hearing about how hard life was and how meaningful Sonoco’s support had been, I wanted to help make a difference.”


As the mentorship coordinator, she noted, “Youth to Mentors is a success because of the Sonoco team members who have fully invested in their student mentees.” As hourly production workers, the mentors serve as a positive example of adults who are steadily employed or who have turned their lives around to students who may not have other positive role models in their lives.


**Boiler Operator, Marcel Smith** described, “This year, I worked with a kid whose father was in prison and had no real father figure. When I started, he never smiled and looked miserable. After getting to know him, his face lit up when he saw me.”


Crouch recognizes the commitment and sacrifice mentoring requires of hourly workers. She explained, “Their work is making a huge difference in the students’ lives, and we acknowledge their commitment by rewarding them for each hour they invest in connecting with the students through this Sonoco program.”


Supported by the school’s principal, the Youth to Leader mentors help students build relationships in a safe school environment over a game of basketball, a board game or a simple conversation. **Power Plant Control Room Operator, Ralf Scott** described, “I enjoy seeing the kids freely talk to someone who will listen. Hearing from their parents about how excited they are to spend time with me makes me grateful.”


### **Doing the Right Thing in Hartsville and Beyond**


“Sonoco In Action isn’t about programs on paper. It’s about people,” explained Chief Human Resources Officer Andrea White. Sonoco team members mentor more than 65 students and support 19 local schools in our hometown of Hartsville, South Carolina, but the company has long-term plans to expand Sonoco In Action charitable efforts across all global facilities, demonstrating our commitment to *Better Packaging. Better Life* .®


Learn more about how we’re[investing in our Sonoco communities](https://www.sonoco.com/sustainability/social) .
